source_notes.finding: No stubs or generated declarations. Every other registered tool (minus any programmatic_tool_caller instance) becomes an async host function in Monty's external_lookup dict, keyword arguments only, with a `_` alias for names that are not identifiers. The run_code-style tool description is static prose that lists no tools; the model learns tool signatures from the agent's normal tool list, where every tool also stays callable directly.

All tools upfront: the model sees every tool's schema as an ordinary tool plus the static PTC description. No search or lazy loading inside the code; allowed_tools only narrows what the code may call. Does not scale past 100 tools without the full schemas in the prompt.

Monty pauses at an external call; pydantic_monty's feed_run awaits the host coroutine, which runs the tool through the agent's ToolExecutor._stream with a copy of the parent invocation_state (so Cedar or risk-policy interventions apply, and an approval interrupt becomes a RuntimeError). Results are unwrapped to dict/list/str. Tool code and credentials stay in the host process; only arguments and results cross to the worker.

Language-level sandbox, stated as such: Monty's VM has no filesystem, env, network, FFI or process access and runs in a separate worker process; the docs warn it bounds the code, not the tools. Probes agree: P3 not-defined, P4 PermissionError, P5 os.environ unsupported, all three P12 attempts fail (no __class__, no __import__).

Only print() output reaches the model, as the ToolResult text; the last expression value is dropped. Capped at 200,000 chars with a visible truncation marker; on error, printed output and the error share the cap with at least half reserved for the error.

VM limits are hardcoded (60 s VM time, 256 MiB, 1000 suspensions); the only tunables are the wall-clock timeout (default 900 s, None disables it) and allowed_tools. The wall-clock timeout cancels the run and the worker stops with it (out/timeout_check.txt).
Fresh per call: a new AsyncMonty pool and session per programmatic_tool_caller invocation, no persistence or snapshots. P8 fresh.

Errors return status 'error' with 'Execution error:' plus Monty's traceback display (file <python-input-0>, line, caret, message), prefixed by anything printed before the failure; syntax errors as 'Syntax error:'; wall-clock timeouts as 'timed out after N seconds.'

On by default in create_harness (default builtin_tools list). Inner calls share a 10-slot semaphore. A programmatic_tool_caller is never exposed to another's code, so no nested runs. The TypeScript harness (harness-ts) has its own implementation, not probed here.

surprises: If the host process exits abruptly (os._exit) while guest code spins, the `monty subprocess` worker is orphaned to PID 1 and keeps burning a core until Monty's own 60 s VM limit ends it; a SIGKILL to the host's process group does take it down. Evidence research/probes/strands-codemode/out/orphan_check.txt. Two such orphans from a side check had to be killed by hand during this run.

The docs say the worker has 'memory, time, and recursion limits', but none of them is configurable: _LIMITS is a module constant. The documented per-tool config (allowed_tools, timeout) only adds a wall clock, so the hardened run cannot lower the 256 MiB memory cap.
Docs and the tool description say only print() output returns; confirmed. A last-expression value is silently dropped (P2), unlike Pydantic AI Harness CodeMode, which returns both.

strands-harness pins pydantic-monty==0.0.23, a much older Monty line than the 1.6.0 used by pydantic-ai-harness 0.71.0 and fastmcp CodeMode in this repo. Same isolation results here, but fixes in later Monty releases do not reach Strands until the pin moves.
`time` is not importable (Pclock: ModuleNotFoundError), so the SPEC's in-sandbox P9 timing cannot run; P9 is timed from host-side call spans. The tool description lists `datetime` as importable.
